page: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v6 is an arm64 virtual machine belonging to the Dpldsv6 series, configured with 16 dedicated physical cores based on the Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 microarchitecture clocked at 3.4 GHz. Operating with one hardware thread per core, the configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 32.0 GB, yielding a 2.0 GB per core allocation that represents a compute-dense 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Fast direct-attached storage is integrated via a 944 GB NVMe SSD, while GPU acceleration is not present on this instance type.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory throughput and data compression speeds. Large-block uncached read throughput registers at 307.54 GB/sec and uncached write throughput reaches 124.58 GB/sec, placing the memory subsystem within the top quartile of tested instances. Single-threaded gzip compression also records top-tier results at 33.08 GB/sec. Across general compute metrics, performance sits securely in the median range, with Geekbench yielding scores of 1,688.0 for single-core execution and 14,736.0 for multi-core scaling. Redis operations deliver 32.07 million SET operations per second, and static web serving achieves 27.37 GB/sec throughput. In contrast, medium-scale 7B parameter LLM prompt processing achieves 24.62 tokens per second, reflecting the bottom quartile.

From an architectural standpoint, the 1:2 memory-to-core ratio and direct-attached NVMe storage provide high core density and fast local disk access without incurring overhead for unneeded RAM. This trade-off suits computational and I/O-intensive pipelines that process data in streams rather than holding massive datasets entirely in memory. Primary operational targets include CI/CD build agents, software compilation, batch processing, static web serving clusters, and caching layers with local ephemeral persistence requirements.
description: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v6 is an arm64 instance powered by 16 dedicated Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 cores clocked at 3.4 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of memory and a bundled 944 GB NVMe SSD. Featuring a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and 128 MB of L3 cache, the system targets compute density over deep memory capacity. Empirical testing shows top-quartile performance in uncached memory bandwidth and single-threaded gzip compression, alongside consistent median output in multi-core compilation, Redis key-value workloads, and static web serving. While less suited for large in-memory datasets or mid-sized LLM prompt processing due to the 2.0 GB per core ceiling, the integrated fast NVMe disk and dedicated ARM execution cores offer strong efficiency for continuous integration pipelines, web tiers, and parallel batch workloads.
